This repo AUTHORS and DISTRIBUTES the FM #28 gate (bin/_manifest.py:54 ships starter-kit/context_budget.py -> adopter context_budget.py, :60 ships the seed -> adopter .context-budget.json) and until now had never configured it for itself — the same blind-at-home shape as BL-29 and upstream issue #59, arriving through configuration rather than path resolution. Run: python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py (there is no root copy of the tool here; see _tool_location below).
_tool_location: The tool is NOT at this repo's root. bin/_manifest.py installs it at ADOPTER roots; canonically it lives only at starter-kit/context_budget.py. Two consequences, both measured not assumed: (1) invoke it as `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py` — find_root() then walks up to this repo root via .git and reads this file, which is why a root-relative `path` below still resolves; (2) `install-hook` would write a hook that execs $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/context_budget.py, which does not exist here, AND this clone already sets core.hooksPath=.githooks whose pre-commit is the FM #27 ledger gate, so install-hook correctly declines with 'already exists and is not ours'. The budget gate is therefore MEASURING here, not BLOCKING. Wiring it into .githooks/pre-commit would edit a canonical file that ships upstream — deliberately not done here; raised as a follow-on instead.
_bytes_per_token: MEASURED ON THIS REPO, 2026-08-15 (S90). Regression of each session's opening context on the size of CLAUDE.md at that session's start, over n=75 transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/-Users-rmsharp-Development-methodology: opening_tokens ~= 42,033.2 + 0.356891 x bytes, R^2 = 0.8083 => 2.8020 B/tok, rounded here to 2.80. Corroborated by two independent local instruments: the same fit with only the lineage defect corrected gives 2.93 (R^2 = 0.6854), and the natural experiment across commit 7603f10 (CLAUDE.md 52,909 -> 8,519 B, -44,390 B) using the two sessions bracketing it within 20 minutes on each side gives 44,390 B / 17,616 tok = 2.52. Three local estimates spanning 2.52-2.93, and the seed's 2.93 from a different project, all agree within ~15%. THE TOOL NOW AGREES — BL-38 FIXED IT (S91, 2026-08-15). The warning that used to live in this key said `--calibrate` prints 14.45 B/tok at R^2 = 0.0513 and must not be adopted; that is no longer true and the key would otherwise have become a false claim about a tool that had been repaired. The two defects behind it (D1: `git log -- CLAUDE.md` walked ALL merged ancestry, so upstream's own CLAUDE.md lineage interleaved with this fork's by commit date and 'size at time T' stopped being a function; D2: ISO timestamps were sorted and compared AS STRINGS across mixed offsets) are fixed in starter-kit/context_budget.py. Re-run `python3 starter-kit/context_budget.py --calibrate` rather than trusting this sentence: at n=76 it prints 2.81 B/tok at R^2 = 0.8054, against the 2.80 recorded here from S90's n=75. The small drift is the extra transcript, not a disagreement. A fit below R^2 = 0.50 is now REFUSED by the tool rather than printed, so this key can no longer be 'corrected' to noise by a session that reads the number and not the statistic.
_fixed_harness_tokens: MEASURED — the intercept of the same n=75 fit above: the opening context that exists before any budgeted file is loaded (system prompt, tool schemas, skill listings, MCP server tools, agent-level memory). The seed carries 35,700 from a different project and a different harness configuration; this repo's floor is higher. Note what this makes CLAUDE.md worth: at 11,064 B and 2.80 B/tok it is 3,951 tok, 9.4% of this floor.
_growth_run: INHERITED FROM THE SEED, NOT DERIVED — and labelled so rather than presented as measured. It cannot be calibrated on day one: this repo has no .context-budget-history.jsonl until this config's first run, so the series the trigger reads is empty. Revisit once ~15 measurements exist; the honest input is how many consecutive non-shrinking readings this repo actually produces between deliberate reductions (S23, S24, S25, S87 and S89 were all reductions, so the true run length here is probably short).

resident._: Resident is a ONE-FILE class in this repo — CLAUDE.md is the only artifact the harness injects in full before the session starts; this repo has no root SESSION_RUNNER.md (its runner is the distributed starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md) and no root SESSION_NOTES.md (its continuity record is HANDOFFS.md). So this total equals CLAUDE.md's own ceiling by construction. That is deliberate and it is NOT a check that cannot fail: the per-file ceiling cannot see a SECOND resident file being added, and this one can. Agent-level memory (~/.claude/projects/.../MEMORY.md) is genuinely resident too but is per-operator and per-machine, outside this repo, and not a reviewable diff — deliberately excluded, and worth remembering when reading the 42,033-tok floor above, which INCLUDES it.

structure.why: CLAUDE.md's own Versioning section states that this heading must stay put because existing CLAUDE.md#versioning links resolve to it; the v3.7-era extraction to docs/RELEASE_HISTORY.md kept the heading for exactly that reason. files._: max_lines 200 is THIS FRAMEWORK'S OWN PUBLISHED NUMBER, not an invention: starter-kit/BOOTSTRAP.md:199 says 'Claude Code targets roughly 200 lines' and tells adopters to extract to a referenced PROJECT_LEARNINGS.md before that budget is crowded. Dogfooding it here is the whole point of BL-37. max_bytes converts it at this file's measured density — 11,064 B / 119 lines = 92.97 B/line, x200 = 18,594 B, rounded to 18,600 — because a line ceiling alone just produces longer lines. warn_bytes sits 2,600 B below, which is two of the largest single-session increases this file has actually taken since the S24 cut (+1,308 B at d69f7a9, +1,017 B at 316e7ef), so the warning arrives with about two sessions of notice. NO protected_fence IS DECLARED, deliberately: the seed's budget:protected fence does not exist in this file, and declaring it without adding it would report 'over' for a missing fence — a red manufactured by this config rather than a real defect. Adding the fence edits canonical content that ships upstream; raised as a follow-on instead.

NO max_line_bytes, deliberately — see HANDOFFS.md below, same reason. **DECOUPLED FROM THE TRIMMER, S116 (2026-08-26), Phase C2.** The sentence above is now HISTORY, not a live derivation: option C1 raised `methodology_trim.py`'s `DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES` 65,536 -> 196,608 B, and this ceiling deliberately did NOT follow it. The two answer different questions -- this one asks what Phase 0 pays to read the file, the trimmer's asks whether archiving is worth doing -- and they merely happened to share a number until now. **65,536 is therefore this fork's own number from here on and needs its own defence when someone next re-opens it.** Two further corrections while this sentence is being rewritten: the `:69` citation was already stale (the constant is at `:127`), and **the claim that BL-9 measured against this number is impossible** -- BL-9 closed 2026-08-01 and the constant was first written 2026-08-03 (`df381ea`); design section 5.4 calibrates it on 52,927 B, which is BL-9's own output commit `7a71df0`, so BL-9 is the constant's INPUT. files._: Read-mandated: Phase 0 step 6 reconciles this file's frontier and Phase 3A reads the predecessor's receipt in full. max_lines 1,200 is THIS FILE'S OWN DECLARED TRIGGER, stated in its front matter ('Archive again ... when this one approaches ~1,200 lines'), which is tighter than the 2,000-line Read cap and so governs. MAX_BYTES 65,536 IS RETAINED BUT NO LONGER THE OPERATIVE GUARD, and S98 measured why. Across 81 transcripts of this repo (the measuring session excluded, heredoc bodies stripped, classified per PIPELINE so `git show f | grep x` counts once): the live root ledger was read WHOLE into a session's context exactly ONCE and read in PART 593 times -- median span 25 lines, largest ever requested 220, against a 452-line file. No read in the corpus asked for even half of it. So the whole-file ceiling guards a cost paid once in 81 sessions, while the cost paid 593 times -- one RECORD, which is what the sentence above already said Phase 3A reads -- had no guard at all. THE GUARD IS NOW `RECORD_BUDGET_BYTES = 12288` IN bin/check-handoff (CANONICAL-ONLY, not in bin/_manifest.py), scoped to the record being written, with the evidence and the fit assertion beside the constant. IT IS A POLICY NUMBER, NOT A DERIVATION -- and that changed at S106 (2026-08-25). It was 18 KiB, derived as (65,536 - 8,000) / 3 = 19,178 rounded down, a formula that fits the budget TO the ceiling and so sized it as large as would fit; steady state 3 x 18 KiB + 8,000 = 63,296 B, only 2,240 B of slack, which forced a trim nearly every session while never touching the ~25 KB a session actually pays. The formula's only remaining job is the assertion 3 x budget + header reserve <= 65,536: 3 x 12,288 + 8,000 = 44,864 B, 68.5% of the ceiling, 20,672 B of slack -- more than one whole receipt. 12,288 was chosen because a receipt's FENCED fields mean 12,108 B while its TRAILING PROSE (the Phase 3A/3B essays, additive to the six mandatory requirements) is 27-30% of it, so the cut lands on the essays; ratified by the operator over costed alternatives 10,240 and 8,192, evidence in docs/planning/record-budget-reduction-plan.md. The floor of 3 is bin/tests.sh Test 34's, not the methodology's. Records have grown 3.15x: oldest 10 mean 5,478 B, newest 10 mean 17,258 B, largest ever 21,267 B (n=104, live + archives). WHY THE CEILING STAYS AND IS NOT LOWERED TO MATCH: it is what the derivation is computed FROM, and it is still the trim trigger -- `methodology_trim.py --file HANDOFFS.md --check` keys on it. Under the OLD derived reading, lowering it would silently re-derive the record budget downward on the next read of this note; that mechanism is gone now that the budget is policy, but the trim-trigger reason stands on its own. Its source is `methodology_trim.py`'s DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES at :80 (this entry said :69 until S98; S97 flagged the drift and left it, FM #17 -- the CHANGELOG.md entry's copy of the same stale citation is UNTOUCHED and still reads :69). EXPECT THIS ENTRY TO REPORT over WHENEVER A CLOSE-OUT HAS JUST APPENDED A RECEIPT AND NO TRIM HAS RUN YET -- that is the trim trigger doing its job, not a defect; the durable question is whether the RECORD budget is green. NO max_line_bytes, deliberately and unlike the seed's SESSION_NOTES.md entry: the handoff block format is one field per line by design, so field lines run to thousands of bytes legitimately, and a per-line ceiling here would fight the format bin/check-handoff enforces rather than find a defect. **DECOUPLED FROM THE TRIMMER, S116 (2026-08-26), Phase C2 -- AND ONE CLAUSE ABOVE IS NOW FALSE.** *"it is still the trim trigger -- `methodology_trim.py --file HANDOFFS.md --check` keys on it"* no longer holds: option C1 raised `DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES` to 196,608 B and Phase C2 gave root Class A ledgers a 196,608 B archive arm, so `--check` on this file now reports **trigger does not fire** at sizes that fired yesterday. The ceiling is kept at 65,536 anyway, for the OTHER reason already stated above -- it is what the A1 fit assertion in `bin/check-handoff` is computed from -- but that is now its ONLY remaining warrant, and the `:80` citation is stale (the constant is at `:127`). **Consequence for the sentence after this one:** an `over` report here right after a close-out is no longer "the trim trigger doing its job"; it is this fork's own read-cost ceiling speaking, and the trimmer will stay silent until 192 KiB. The durable question is unchanged: is the RECORD budget green?

It was ^\*\*BL-[0-9]+ —, the grep this file's header publishes; that grep now reads the DETAIL file and the header says so. The pattern is deliberately anchored on the link into the detail file, so it matches the 19 open-item rows and NOT the §Completed items pointer table beside them, which uses the same **BL-N** bold form. WHY THIS CHECK EARNED ITS KEEP: the split tripped it — the gate reported instrument-failed (worse than over, by its own ordering) the first time it ran against the new shape, which is exactly the announcement a structural instrument exists to make. Note the header's own caveat: BL-16 has no heading of its own, so it has an index row derived by hand rather than from the detail file's headings, and a count taken from the detail file is one lower than the open-item count. That is correct, not a defect.

This entry is what turns BL-37 half (b) — adding a BACKLOG.md entry to the DISTRIBUTED seed, which needs a go-ahead — into an argument from a measurement instead of a guess. **SUPERSEDED IN PART, S99 (2026-08-18): the file is 26,504 B and the breach is CLOSED, by SPLIT rather than by the compaction this entry said would be needed.** The 18 item bodies (81,340 B) moved VERBATIM to docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md, which is read on demand and carries no ceiling — the same shape, and the same argument, as the v3.7 CLAUDE.md → docs/RELEASE_HISTORY.md extraction. Nothing was abandoned, so the operator policy question this entry raises was never reached; it stands unanswered for the day someone wants the DETAIL file smaller too. **AND THE CEILING WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE READ PATTERN BEFORE IT WAS KEPT, not assumed:** across 82 transcripts (S99's own excluded) this file was read WHOLE 23 times in 22 of them — 27% — against 584 partial reads. Its two sibling ledgers were re-derived off the whole-file axis precisely because they measured 1-in-81 (HANDOFFS.md, S98) and 1-in-80 (FRAMEWORK_LEARNINGS.md, S97); this file is read whole ~22x more often than either, so the whole-file ceiling is the right axis here and was RETAINED. files._: RE-DERIVED 2026-08-26 (S114), 65,536 -> 73,728 B (72 KiB), on the operator's decision from four costed BL-45 options (raise / archive / compact / split). CANONICAL-ONLY: the distributed seed starter-kit/context-budget.json declares CLAUDE.md, SESSION_NOTES.md and LEARNINGS.md and NOT this file, so no adopter is affected -- checked by reading the seed, not assumed. WHY THE OLD VALUE WAS REPLACED RATHER THAN RAISED: 65,536 was never derived for this file. It was borrowed from the ledgers' DEFAULT_BUDGET_BYTES, and the justification that stood here converted it to tokens at bytes_per_token = 2.80 and compared the result to a 42,033-token OPENING-CONTEXT floor -- two mistakes now measured. (1) That estimator answers a different question: it fits opening context against CLAUDE.md's size, and re-running its own --calibrate returns 2.46 at R^2 0.59 today, a -12% drift in eleven days. (2) The limit that actually bites a read is the agent Read cap, ~25,000 TOKENS, not a share of opening context. The old note's arithmetic gave 23,406 tok for a 65,536 B file; measured, this content is 21,623 tok at that size -- an 8% overstatement, in the direction that made the ceiling look tighter than it was. THE MEASUREMENT, and re-run it rather than trusting these numbers. Concatenate this file with itself, Read the doubled file with a spanning `limit`, and halve the token count the error reports -- an over-cap explicit limit returns NO content and costs nothing:   cat F F > /tmp/x.txt   # then Read /tmp/x.txt with offset=1 limit=<its line count> x2 = 131,040 B -> 43,247 tok; x3 = 196,560 B -> 64,868 tok against 64,870 predicted, so the estimator is linear here to 0.004%. This content runs 3.0300 B/token, and the one-read cliff is 25,000 x 3.0300 = 75,751 B. WHY 73,728 AND NOT THE CLIFF, and this part is JUDGMENT, labelled: a ceiling must sit below the point where the file stops fitting, not on it. 75,751 leaves zero margin and assumes every future row is as sparse as today's. Rows carry paths, identifiers and code spans, which tokenise worse. 73,728 is the ceiling at which the file stays inside one read even if EVERY new byte is 20% denser than today's content (24,332 tok filled at today's density; 25,010 at 20% denser, which is within the estimator's own noise). It is also a round 72 KiB, consistent with this repo's style. WHAT THIS BOUGHT, measured after the fact rather than estimated: 8,192 B. The four owed rows were written in the same session and cost 4,159 B (968-1,148 B each, all well inside the 1,500 B budget), leaving 4,045 B = about THREE more rows. The pre-write estimate said 'nearer ONE' by assuming every row would fill its budget; they did not, and the estimate is corrected here rather than left standing. RE-MEASURED AFTER THE APPEND, because adding content can move the ratio the ceiling was derived from: 69,683 B -> 22,926 tok = 3.0396 B/token, marginally LESS dense than the 3.0300 the ceiling was set from, so the margin held and the file sits 2,074 tokens under the cap. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX -- THE GROWTH, and Learning #26 is the reason. The 37 rows are 97% of the file and the front matter forbids editing them, so the untouchable remainder IS the file; no reduction step can reach it. The real question underneath is a POLICY one -- how many learnings should the framework carry before old ones retire -- and no ceiling answers it. BL-45's other three options remain open and are costed in that item: archiving the oldest 10 rows frees 7,589 B and orphans only 5 citations in 2 distributed files (the checker's sweep covers the DISTRIBUTED corpus only -- 8 citations across 4 files -- not the 471 that exist overall); compacting the 20 rows that exceed the row budget frees 17,533 B but edits an append-only record. STILL TRUE AND CARRIED FORWARD FROM S97's NOTE: this file was read WHOLE 1 time in 80 transcripts and read in PART 243 times, so a whole-file ceiling guards a rarely-paid cost while the cost actually paid is PER ROW. The primary guard is therefore bin/check-learnings' ROW_BUDGET_BYTES = 1500 (CANONICAL-ONLY, so no adopter has it), scoped to rows not yet frozen in git HEAD, pinned by bin/tests.sh Test 37 with 9 assertions and 4 mutants. NO max_line_bytes here, deliberately: a per-row cap set anywhere useful is red on day one against rows nobody may edit. RE-OPEN THIS when the five rows are spent -- which is S97's own instruction, and it is what brought the value here.

_synced: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, and this is an inversion worth stating rather than an omission. The seed ships two synced entries (SESSION_RUNNER.md, SAFEGUARDS.md) that drift-check an adopter's local copy against a canonical checkout elsewhere. THIS REPO IS THAT CANONICAL. It holds no local copies to drift — starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md ARE the originals — so the naive adaptation, pointing path and canonical at the same file, would git hash-object the same blob twice and compare it to itself: an assertion of an identity that no change can falsify, which is the exact 'comment shaped like a guard' this repo has already had to delete once (Learning #16). The other half of the inversion also holds: the seed says synced files are drift-checked and never size-checked because an adopter may not edit them, so a size finding would be unactionable — here they ARE editable, so a size finding WOULD be actionable, and starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md is 52,386 B and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md 15,386 B, both read at every adopter's Phase 0. Ceilings for them are a framework-policy decision that constrains future canonical work and would ship upstream; NOT taken here (FM #17), measured and raised instead.
_deliberate_exclusions: Measured and left out on purpose, with the numbers a future session needs: starter-kit/SESSION_RUNNER.md 52,386 B (Phase 0 mandates it for every adopter) and starter-kit/SAFEGUARDS.md 15,386 B (Phase 0 step 1, 'in full, not skimmed') — both distributed, see _synced. README.md 89,175 B and ITERATIVE_METHODOLOGY.md 68,240 B — large, but read on demand and by humans, not mandated at Phase 0. docs/RELEASE_HISTORY.md — the sibling the v3.7 CLAUDE.md extraction created, read on demand. docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md 86,086 B — the sibling the S99 BACKLOG.md split created, same shape and same reason: opened only once a session knows which item it is working on. Its losslessness is proved by docs/planning/BACKLOG-DETAIL.md.verify.sh, not by a ceiling. Adding any of these means declaring a ceiling nobody has defended yet, which is policy, not provisioning.
